Scattered across Missouri, and the rest of America I'm sure, are thousands of working-class communities that no one ever thinks about. Their curbs crumble into the streets. Their sidewalks, when they have them, are cracked and jagged. The people who run this country, the Wall Street bankers, the politicians, the corporate executives, don't see those of us who live there. Instead, they see loans, consumers, votes, labor, and occasional cannon fodder. If they looked closer, and chose to make decisions based on our country rather than on themselves, they would discover a reservoir of strength and resiliency that they could organize into conquering every challenge we face.
I know because I grew up in one of these neighborhoods. First on a short street called Cottage Lane, and then a block away on Dunklin Street, in Jefferson City, Missouri. It was a beautiful place to live. All of us kids running in and out of each other's houses. Black, white, brown. It didn't matter, we were there together and took care of one another when things went sideways.
I turned eight years old in the midst of all this awesomeness. I remember it well, because it was going to be my best birthday ever -- I was going to get a little sister! There were already three of us kids but, seeing as my parents were passionately Catholic at the time, we were born in fairly quick succession and rapidly vacillated between friends and enemies. A couple devastating miscarriages later, and we were going to have a little sister we could spend all our time doting and loving on.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d51d02e-179d-4f89-b306-f7c315570264?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
My mother kept saying it was the easiest pregnancy ever, and we counted the days excitedly. Two days before my birthday, she was born. We talked to my parents on the phone. Easiest one yet, my mom proclaimed, the timing was perfect, they hoped to be home for a birthday party. I really was getting a little sister for my birthday this year!
After school, my grandma hurried us to the hospital to meet our new little sister. We each got to hold her as doctors and nurses hustled this way and that. My mom and dad were tense. They told us our little sister just needed a few tests run. Before we knew it, my little sister was on a helicopter to St. Louis, my parents following closely behind in our van. She was on the verge of dying and needed open heart surgery.
That birthday did end up being memorable, but for all the wrong reasons. As an eight-year-old kid, it's hard not to be selfish, and I remember wondering how, if my sister died on my birthday, would I ever really get a birthday again? We never did extravagant presents as kids, since times were always tight, but every year my mom or grandma would make us a special themed cake. A baseball, a cat, a clown holding balloons... something meaningful for us.
That year, however, my grandma drove me to the grocery store and told me I could pick out any cake I wanted. I was sad, but also kind of excited -- I spent hours as a kid ogling the grocery store desserts and wondering what they were like. I walked up and down the display, looking for the biggest brightest smash of frosting I could find. When I finally saw it, I just knew. It was a beautiful white cake with a massive pile of red flowers flowing out of one corner.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f96f7f09-25ae-4e1a-a0b3-b6dba404cf45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
"Are you sure?" My grandma asked, as I told her it was the one. "It's not really a birthday cake. But if you want it..."
Oh, I wanted it.
I don't remember what present I got that year. But I remember eating every single ounce of that red flower frosting. How the red dye stained my fingers. And I remember how ridiculously sick I felt after gorging myself and how I swore I would never eat a bite of frosting again as long as I lived. An oath I'm sure I broke at the next family birthday. Although, to this day I don't go heavy on icing and have flashbacks if I try.
My sister survived that open heart surgery, several ensuing health scares, another open-heart surgery, and more. It's hard to capture the toll that takes on a family. Mentally, emotionally, and financially. I remember my mom crying herself to sleep not just because she wasn't sure if her little girl would survive, but also because she had no idea how they were going to make it financially. Something that we could have never accomplished alone, and only did because we had a community behind us.
For years our mechanic, W, took care of us no matter what ability my parents had to pay at the time. When my parents were run completely dry, a man down at church did their bankruptcy for free. During the time they had to spend at the hospital 150 miles away while my sister fought to survive, people around town took us other kids into their homes and cared for us.
It was during one of these periods, when my parents were away, that the people in our community, many of whom we didn't even know, did something remarkable to help our family. Something that got them no glory, when they could have just gone about their day without anyone knowing any differently.
Us three other kids were farmed out across town while our little sister was hospitalized in St. Louis, my parents at her side. They were completely broke at the time, waiting on the next paycheck,, and worried about how they were even going to get back home. They pushed it out of their minds, praying for the best, and near the end of that hospitalization they got an unexpected call from a member of my mom's prayer group. The group, knowing what we were going through, had collected some money to help us get through.
My dad agreed to stay at the hospital so that my mom could go back, pick up the money, see us kids, and get the house ready for him and our little sister to return.
Feeling lighter than she had in months, my mom rolled into town on fumes. With tears and hugs she accepted the generous gift, filled up at the gas station three doors down from our house, and made a beeline for the store. For the first time in a long time she would be able to get everything she needed.
She took her time filling up the cart, picked out ingredients for our favorite meals, and daydreamed about how she would surprise us since we didn't know she was in town.
On the way to the register, she stopped in an aisle to look at something for one of my siblings. While her back was to the cart, someone grabbed her purse and ran off with it. The only money she had in the world was in that purse. Food for her kids. Heat. Water. Gas. The joy of our reunion. All gone.
She frantically told the manager. They called the police. She could hardly tell the officer a thing, she was sobbing too uncontrollably. Eventually, between her broken replies to his questions and the manager's interjections, he pieced together what had happened. He searched the area and found her purse in the restroom.
He handed it back to her. Everything was there, except the money.
He stood back and copied the information from my mom's driver's license, now that she had it back, while she collected herself.
"Is everything on here right?" he asked, "In case something turns up?"
"Yes," she sobbed, taking it back from him. He walked her to the car.
"Everything's going to be ok, ma'am," he said as she got in, "It'll work out."
She nodded, feeling like there was no way it would ever work out, closed the door, and drove home. Empty handed.
She says it was the darkest moment of her life, which hadn't been particularly easy. Her husband was hours away at a hospital with their little girl clinging to life. She had nothing to offer the other three of us, so she didn't even call to say she was in town. What do you do when you receive charity and then lose it? Where else is there to turn?
The phone rang. She answered out of habit. Her friend Joni was on the other line. My mom broke down immediately and told her friend what had happened. That she just needed to be alone. And she laid down. She laid there that afternoon. Ignoring the world. Ignoring the phone if it rang. She drifted into a haze.
She woke that evening to the sound of the doorbell ringing. Groggily, she debated whether or not to answer it. Before she could decide, there was a banging at the door.
"Coming..." she warbled, and made her way to the door, tear streaked and bedraggled.
When she opened it up, the policeman was standing there.
"I'm sorry to bother you ma'am," he apologized, "but I wanted to come check on you, after everything you've been going through. And make sure you're ok."
"Thank you," she replied, "I think I'll be ok," she added, trying to smooth her hair and wipe away her tears so that he would believe her.
The officer nodded.
"I think so, too," he said, handing her an envelope. "From some of us down at the station. Just to be sure."
My mom gave him a puzzled look.
"Well, good-bye now," he said, and walked away.
"Bye."
My mom closed the door and looked in the envelope. The officer had spent the afternoon collecting from guys he worked with. And he wasn't the only one. The father of my mom's friend, Joni, lived about thirty minutes away and had spent that afternoon collecting from his neighbors and members of his church. That night he brought the collection by. And so did others. Word had gotten around and the people in our community made us whole again.
No one would have noticed if they hadn't and many of those who contributed didn't even know who we were. They just knew that we were in need, and there was enough extra in our community in those days for people to take care of one another.
Despite the hardship, it was a beautiful time. For months acquaintances, strangers, and friends brought food by the house. More than we could ever eat. I sat on the couch in the evenings and watched it roll in, meeting so many new people and feeling their love. They took care of us. Lasagna, spaghetti, casseroles... Goodness gracious, the casseroles! I remember sitting on the couch and praying one day after a particularly long string of casseroles: "Dear God, please, please, let someone bring a lasagna tonight!"
Most of the people who helped us had no more money than we did. They, too, were living paycheck to paycheck and knew that if disaster struck -- a car accident, a temporary layoff, a broken boiler, a medical emergency -- it could easily be them. But they helped us anyway.
That spirit still lives here. Many years later, W's mechanic shop, the shop where they had helped my parents and so many like us, was drowned by a freak flood. The property didn't require flood insurance, and everything he had in that establishment, his entire life and existence, was destroyed. The community came together and rebuilt it. And he's still there, taking care of the next generation of families.
I don't pray for lasagna anymore. I pray that our leaders finally find the courage to make decisions that support communities like Jefferson City's east side, rather than decisions that support their campaign donors who strip our communities for parts and leave us less capable of taking care of one another.

A couple devastating miscarriages later, and we were going to have a little sister we could spend all our time doting and loving on. | | ---|---|--- My mother kept saying it was the easiest pregnancy ever, and we counted the days excitedly. Two days before my birthday, she was born. We talked to my parents on the phone. Easiest one yet, my mom proclaimed, the timing was perfect, they hoped to be home for a birthday party. I really was getting a little sister for my birthday this year! After school, my grandma hurried us to the hospital to meet our new little sister. We each got to hold her as doctors and nurses hustled this way and that. My mom and dad were tense. They told us our little sister just needed a few tests run. Before we knew it, my little sister was on a helicopter to St. Louis, my parents following closely behind in our van. She was on the verge of dying and needed open heart surgery. That birthday did end up being memorable, but for all the wrong reasons. As an eight-year-old kid, it's hard not to be selfish, and I remember wondering how, if my sister died on my birthday, would I ever really get a birthday again? We never did extravagant presents as kids, since times were always tight, but every year my mom or grandma would make us a special themed cake. A baseball, a cat, a clown holding balloons... something meaningful for us. That year, however, my grandma drove me to the grocery store and told me I could pick out any cake I wanted. I was sad, but also kind of excited -- I spent hours as a kid ogling the grocery store desserts and wondering what they were like. I walked up and down the display, looking for the biggest brightest smash of frosting I could find. When I finally saw it, I just knew. It was a beautiful white cake with a massive pile of red flowers flowing out of one corner. | | ---|---|--- "Are you sure?" My grandma asked, as I told her it was the one. "It's not really a birthday cake. But if you want it..." Oh, I wanted it. I don't remember what present I got that year. But I remember eating every single ounce of that red flower frosting. How the red dye stained my fingers. And I remember how ridiculously sick I felt after gorging myself and how I swore I would never eat a bite of frosting again as long as I lived. An oath I'm sure I broke at the next family birthday. Although, to this day I don't go heavy on icing and have flashbacks if I try. My sister survived that open heart surgery, several ensuing health scares, another open-heart surgery, and more. It's hard to capture the toll that takes on a family. Mentally, emotionally, and financially. I remember my mom crying herself to sleep not just because she wasn't sure if her little girl would survive, but also because she had no idea how they were going to make it financially. Something that we could have never accomplished alone, and only did because we had a community behind us. For years our mechanic, W, took care of us no matter what ability my parents had to pay at the time. When my parents were run completely dry, a man down at church did their bankruptcy for free. During the time they had to spend at the hospital 150 miles away while my sister fought to survive, people around town took us other kids into their homes and cared for us. It was during one of these periods, when my parents were away, that the people in our community, many of whom we didn't even know, did something remarkable to help our family. Something that got them no glory, when they could have just gone about their day without anyone knowing any differently. Us three other kids were farmed out across town while our little sister was hospitalized in St. Louis, my parents at her side. They were completely broke at the time, waiting on the next paycheck,, and worried about how they were even going to get back home. They pushed it out of their minds, praying for the best, and near the end of that hospitalization they got an unexpected call from a member of my mom's prayer group. The group, knowing what we were going through, had collected some money to help us get through. My dad agreed to stay at the hospital so that my mom could go back, pick up the money, see us kids, and get the house ready for him and our little sister to return. Feeling lighter than she had in months, my mom rolled into town on fumes. With tears and hugs she accepted the generous gift, filled up at the gas station three doors down from our house, and made a beeline for the store. For the first time in a long time she would be able to get everything she needed. She took her time filling up the cart, picked out ingredients for our favorite meals, and daydreamed about how she would surprise us since we didn't know she was in town. On the way to the register, she stopped in an aisle to look at something for one of my siblings. While her back was to the cart, someone grabbed her purse and ran off with it. The only money she had in the world was in that purse. Food for her kids. Heat. Water. Gas. The joy of our reunion. All gone. She frantically told the manager. They called the police. She could hardly tell the officer a thing, she was sobbing too uncontrollably. Eventually, between her broken replies to his questions and the manager's interjections, he pieced together what had happened. He searched the area and found her purse in the restroom. He handed it back to her. Everything was there, except the money. He stood back and copied the information from my mom's driver's license, now that she had it back, while she collected herself. "Is everything on here right?" he asked, "In case something turns up?" "Yes," she sobbed, taking it back from him. He walked her to the car. "Everything's going to be ok, ma'am," he said as she got in, "It'll work out." She nodded, feeling like there was no way it would ever work out, closed the door, and drove home. Empty handed. She says it was the darkest moment of her life, which hadn't been particularly easy. Her husband was hours away at a hospital with their little girl clinging to life. She had nothing to offer the other three of us, so she didn't even call to say she was in town. What do you do when you receive charity and then lose it? Where else is there to turn? The phone rang. She answered out of habit. Her friend Joni was on the other line. My mom broke down immediately and told her friend what had happened. That she just needed to be alone. And she laid down. She laid there that afternoon. Ignoring the world. Ignoring the phone if it rang. She drifted into a haze. She woke that evening to the sound of the doorbell ringing. Groggily, she debated whether or not to answer it. Before she could decide, there was a banging at the door. "Coming..." she warbled, and made her way to the door, tear streaked and bedraggled. When she opened it up, the policeman was standing there. "I'm sorry to bother you ma'am," he apologized, "but I wanted to come check on you, after everything you've been going through. And make sure you're ok." "Thank you," she replied, "I think I'll be ok," she added, trying to smooth her hair and wipe away her tears so that he would believe her. The officer nodded. "I think so, too," he said, handing her an envelope. "From some of us down at the station. Just to be sure." My mom gave him a puzzled look. "Well, good-bye now," he said, and walked away. "Bye." My mom closed the door and looked in the envelope. The officer had spent the afternoon collecting from guys he worked with. And he wasn't the only one. The father of my mom's friend, Joni, lived about thirty minutes away and had spent that afternoon collecting from his neighbors and members of his church. That night he brought the collection by. And so did others. Word had gotten around and the people in our community made us whole again. No one would have noticed if they hadn't and many of those who contributed didn't even know who we were. They just knew that we were in need, and there was enough extra in our community in those days for people to take care of one another. Despite the hardship, it was a beautiful time. For months acquaintances, strangers, and friends brought food by the house. More than we could ever eat. I sat on the couch in the evenings and watched it roll in, meeting so many new people and feeling their love. They took care of us. Lasagna, spaghetti, casseroles... Goodness gracious, the casseroles! I remember sitting on the couch and praying one day after a particularly long string of casseroles: "Dear God, please, please, let someone bring a lasagna tonight!" Most of the people who helped us had no more money than we did. They, too, were living paycheck to paycheck and knew that if disaster struck -- a car accident, a temporary layoff, a broken boiler, a medical emergency -- it could easily be them. But they helped us anyway. That spirit still lives here. Many years later, W's mechanic shop, the shop where they had helped my parents and so many like us, was drowned by a freak flood. The property didn't require flood insurance, and everything he had in that establishment, his entire life and existence, was destroyed. The community came together and rebuilt it. And he's still there, taking care of the next generation of families. I don't pray for lasagna anymore. I pray that our leaders finally find the courage to make decisions that support communities like Jefferson City's east side, rather than decisions that support their campaign donors who strip our communities for parts and leave us less capable of taking care of one another. He recruited volunteers and personally stood in front of shopping malls and other places with street traffic and obtained the requisite signatures. He then participated in the debate with Republican Tom Foley and Democrat Dan Malloy and accurately told the voters that Connecticut's spending was out of control. Too bad the people did not listen to him because he was correct.

But I can't do that and win this battleground district without you by my side. [**Please, can you split a $15 contribution between Serve America and my campaign to help me start the general election off on the right foot? Every single dollar will help power our pro-democracy movement through Election Day and help us take back the House majority from the extremist GOP.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/90257994/489918316/191792663?refcode=240805&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZDliMjE3ZS00ZjUzLWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRkYmZjNGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8_1l6G2upD5eAndC9E7asxAwkQy88mlgfn13o7doBNo=) The people of Virginia’s 7th district spoke up loud and clear to say that they want a representative with integrity — one who preserves our fundamental values and principles and not extremists who want to ban abortions and books. It’s a fight to defend the very future of our democracy, and the stakes have never been higher. So as we begin this next stage of our pro-democracy movement, I am hoping you will stand firmly by my side — because I cannot fend off attacks from Trump, wealthy MAGA mega-donors, and GOP super PACs without your support. Hey Peter, The dad jokes were flying. The lawn care tips flowed freely. And a fun, diverse group of father-figures was ready to lace up their bright white New Balance sneakers when I joined Pete and Chasten Buttigieg, Governor Tim Walz, and many of my Congressional colleagues at the first Dads for Kamala call this week! Cheesy jokes aside, the stakes for our families in the upcoming election are huge, and **we need to let voters know that Kamala Harris and Democrats are the only ones truly fighting for hardworking, everyday families.** _It was the Biden-Harris Administration and Democrats who passed the Child Tax Credit, lowering taxes for millions of families and lifting millions of kids out of poverty._ _It’s Kamala Harris and Democrats who are fighting for paid family and medical leave — and to lower the costs of childcare nationwide._ _And it’s Kamala Harris and Democrats who'll keep fighting for our children’s freedoms, particularly our daughters’ and granddaughters' freedom to make their own reproductive choices._ In contrast, **Donald Trump and JD Vance want to control when and how parents have kids. Fellow patriot,

A new poll was just released that shows us only 4 points behind shady Sherrod Brown — a man who’s been in political office for 50 YEARS! _**That’s right — five decades of the same tired, swampy politics that have sold out Ohio and our nation.**_

# **JD Vance is Weird**
---
| | | | | [ ](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2udn71-e9qd87-kyd76rh8/)
---
| | | | folks, Let's face it: JD Vance is weird. Saying that political leaders without biological children "don't really have a direct stake" in the country is outlandish, to say the least. His odd viewpoints alienate a significant portion of the population and raise questions about Vance's grasp on reality. The Democrats' new strategy of labeling Trump and Vance as weird seems to be working brilliantly. We have seen in the media that it frustrates opponents, leading them to amplify it further with their off-balance responses. So far, Trump and Vance have been incapable of finding an effective comeback, leaving them scrambling. Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, a potential vice-presidential candidate for Harris, called Trump and Vance "just weird" in a recent interview. The Democratic Governors Association amplified this sentiment, spreading it across social media. Walz even referenced Trump's bizarre habit of mentioning the fictional serial killer Hannibal Lecter from "Silence of the Lambs" in his stump speeches, adding to the weirdness factor. Harris's campaign hasn't missed a beat in highlighting Vance's oddities. In a recent news release, they described Vance's out-of-touch ideas, particularly his stance on abortion and his comments about childless leaders. Harris allies, including Sens. Brian Schatz of Hawaii and Chris Murphy of Connecticut, have also chimed in, calling Vance's past comments "super weird." At her first fundraiser as the likely Democratic nominee, Harris herself called out Trump's "wild lies" and Vance's peculiar statements, reiterating that the only box to put them in is "weird." This new narrative has given Democrats a powerful advantage, one they rarely had when President Biden was still in the race. JD Vance's weirdness isn't a new revelation, either. While the majority of the public is learning who Vance is for the first time through these strange headlines, he has a history of making controversial remarks. In a 2021 interview, Vance slammed prominent childless Democrats, including Harris, as "childless cat ladies" with no stake in America. This comment alone is enough to raise eyebrows and question his judgment. Harris's quip in 2018, when preparing for a potential debate with Trump, sums it up perfectly: "Why are you being so weird? What's wrong with you?" Despite their attempts to flip the script, Trump and Vance have struggled. Trump spokesman Steven Cheung's attempts to redirect the weird label back at Harris and her allies have fallen flat. Donald Trump Jr.'s online rants about "soft on crime" politicians and Vance's reposting of videos criticizing Harris only highlight their desperation. In contrast, Democrats have masterfully co-opted Republican attack lines, using the "weird" label to their advantage. The Republicans' previous tactics of sharing clips of Harris's laugh or her stories have backfired, with Democrats now embracing these moments as in-jokes. The "coconut tree" anecdote has even become a symbol of unity among Harris's supporters. [**_JD Vance's weirdness is not just a political talking point—_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2udn71-e9qd88-kyd76rh9/)[** _Vance and MAGA are clearly out of touch with what Americans want, but that does not mean they are backing down this Novemb_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2udn71-e9qd89-kyd76rh0/) [**_er. name: Bill Eigel for Governor
subject: Election Day is Tomorrow. Vote Bill Eigel for Governor!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Eigel for Missouri, Thomas Hughes, Treasurer_
body:
Tomorrow is election day. I know that in a political campaign, so much gets boiled down into 30-sec ads and soundbites. |
---
| | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/billeigel/eigeltravelsstatekehoeducksdebate-12718685?e=c00a6982d2)
---
|
---
|
---
| | Tomorrow is election day. I know that in a political campaign, so much gets boiled down into 30-second ads and soundbites. So I wanted to write you a substantive note about my intentions as governor. Missouri is a great state. We have so many advantages. First among them is the strength and courage of our people. We have done great things, and can do more. Our greatest weakness, in my humble opinion, is our political class. On the left and right, they have let us down time and time again. It’s because they are consumed by group-think and big money that is totally divorced from the interests of the people. They campaign on one thing, and then do another. And we’re left frustrated and disappointed. It doesn’t have to be this way. In states like Texas, Tennessee, and Florida people are making more money and enjoying the rewards of bold, conservative policies. When Texas and Florida put illegals on buses and shipped them to sanctuary cities, even some weak Republicans there said they were going too far. They held firm. Now, it’s obvious they did the right thing. I’ve got a few simple promises that I’ve discussed in detail throughout this campaign. When I get elected we are going to: End personal property tax so that you don’t have to pay rent to the government on things that you own. 29 other states have done this. So can we. It’s not hard to make up the difference. Deport illegal immigrants living in our state by declaring an invasion under Article IV of the Missouri constitution. My opponent called it “foolish.” I think it’s foolish to let the chaos continue. Secure our elections by returning to the common-sense standard of hand-counted ballots rather than untrustworthy machines. That’s obvious. Of course, there’s more. Replace education bureaucracy with higher-paid teachers in the classroom. Get rid of waste like DEI government spending so we can focus on essential services. Eliminate the income tax. Ban foreign-ownership of Missouri land and return it to the people, because Missouri should enrich Missourians...or at least Americans. I just want to live in a Missouri where the courage and instincts of our politicians match the boldness and intelligence of our people. The good news is: we’re close to making it happen. That's why Trump endorsed our campaign. I’ll fill you in on what our data people are saying. Every model shows this is now a two-way race between our campaign–the conservative grassroots–and Mike Kehoe–the establishment pick. We are tied and surging, while voters are starting to learn about his opposition to deportation and quiet passion for tax hikes. They actually don’t like that stuff. If you’re a RINO, you can’t fool people with your big-money PACs forever. (Ashcroft is plummeting and, at this point, is a wasted vote.) When we win on Tuesday, it will be thanks to an army of grassroots conservative Missourians who stood up and said “No More.” That will ring throughout the halls of our capitol, and they will realize that the people are more powerful than the liberal special interests that have captured that place for so long.

If you read all this, and you’re with that mission: I’m asking you to do one thing for me. Can you text or call ten of your friends–right now–and let them know how you’re voting tomorrow? If just 1,000 of our supporters do this–we cannot lose. It’s more powerful than any ad, mailer, or annoying mass text. In fact, it’s what all good campaigns should look like. The people, not PACs, decide elections. In a tied race like this one, it is very likely to make all the difference.

In Liberty,
Bill Eigel

| | Fellow American, I've played in lots of double-headers. And that's exactly what you and I have on our hands here. A one-on-one matchup with Adam Schiff on November 5th. **[**Can I count on your contribution of $6 to help defeat Adam Schiff today?**](http://links.gopallies.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e37b64e652d84d65a40072608d0a22d5&_e=BgkNF2ONZ_d6rNE7vL6ufMNG5Zfo8NBg7imBwqewtiPlTcPbM2oUK-nsp3t86vT21toGcUxuji7fOgOsNE6NQ_7C6vBdOLp2u5fdik1FOSCUc8pRhUiKFOZQxE6O-6Cyr9kwrWYO66azFjKPbDvLDXGfi33YswcYYAEiWnQneP9iB2-R6kjY0wU5WvP8cUzHxJQMmJAAP5T2_WPSWOm1khBSCnTe2zEZOPLw5tycQRMLwdJ1SiypsOefUCqZWc19KCjUbBtl4NBH_TFlCWV3USkfVGT6v1awTl_GWda0vPHmAaJDWZ9l0Ecf9OEJbAhn-_nS3DXmw-_kM9iw7O5eSghO1FhNfQNEx0Fuo4DfudJkxbJT_yLOaKpCNeGwsC_aIQIeMvLxFDZGMSWN3sG5xw%3D%3D)** You see, Adam Schiff's enablers in the corporate media are already spreading the lie that this race is over. They're saying you and I don't have a chance (just like they did when I entered the race back in October). They're saying that Adam Schiff notched a double victory by advancing to the General Election and drawing me as his opponent. In other words, they're ready, willing and able to cut California voters entirely out of the picture again. My response to Schiff's allies saying they'd rather face me: **_Be careful what you wish for._** I'd liken this to my playing days when a cocky opposing pitcher throws a 94mph fastball right over the plate. I'll tell you, the ball would look as big as a grapefruit before I'd smash it over the fence and touch all the bases on the way home. And look how far we've already made it. I'm in first place in the primary and gaining momentum headed towards the November election. Look, I'm not saying this will be easy. Quite the opposite. It's going to be a nonstop, 58-county fight between now and November 5th. **[That said, I must ask: will you rush a contribution to my senate campaign today?](http://links.gopallies.com/u/click?_t=e3c9a4cac7f248a39c2a3d920479a441&_m=e37b64e652d84d65a40072608d0a22d5&_e=BgkNF2ONZ_d6rNE7vL6ufMNG5Zfo8NBg7imBwqewtiPlTcPbM2oUK-nsp3t86vT21toGcUxuji7fOgOsNE6NQ_7C6vBdOLp2u5fdik1FOSCUc8pRhUiKFOZQxE6O-6Cyr9kwrWYO66azFjKPbDvLDXGfi33YswcYYAEiWnQneP9iB2-R6kjY0wU5WvP8cUzHxJQMmJAAP5T2_WPSWOm1khBSCnTe2zEZOPLw5tycQRMLwdJ1SiypsOefUCqZWc19LQ9k4rxdFo2qX3ti7Vxk1RMmM0hjKvZ7tCLouQgeqhCRUxeipKgUhVLxiqO3_Yh-GgJ24ezePFIGOETnGUBxRshMyXyIgMlXS7HqKlAN0TYdu2rBGa17pZ25BNyZgTnd029Yqh01tdZSsGLwlsj3nQ%3D%3D) ** This is going to be an expensive fight. Hiring staff, recruiting and training volunteers, equipping them with the very best technology to identify our voter and secure their vote by November 5th. There's no time to lose. In closing, I can't help but think how Adam Schiff and his team of high-priced DC consultants thought they were being savvy in trying to make sure I became their opponent in General Election. Reports are they even spent money running ads promoting me. But what they've really done is awaken a sleeping giant here. Remember, before it became a wasteland of crime, homelessness, and sky-high taxes, California was a land of dreamers, a land of opportunity. It was a place where a scrawny little kid could start as a bat boy for his heroes, work hard, win a World Series, and land on a Topps baseball card. California can be that place again. America can be that place again. And it starts with throwing out political liars and connivers like Adam Schiff and reclaiming our freedom roots. Time is the most important factor. Thank you!

| Peter,
When I am elected to serve you in Congress, my first priority will be to secure the border.
Build the Border Wall: I will fight to complete the border wall, hire more Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents, and provide the U.S. Border Patrol with the high-tech equipment they need to do their jobs.
Restore the "Remain in Mexico" Program: I will support a return to the successful "Remain in Mexico" program that required asylum seekers to apply at a U.S. consulate in Mexico and remain in Mexico until their claim was resolved. President Trump created this program; President Biden eliminated it with the stroke of a pen. It's time for Congress to make it law.
End Catch-and-Release: I will end the catch-and-release policy for illegal migrants with pending immigration cases. Far too many have used this loophole to simply disappear and never show up for their court appearance.
Support State Efforts: I will support state efforts like those in Texas to stop illegal migrants. Our border states are on the front lines of an invasion. The federal government should be working with state governors, not against them.
End Amnesty and Sanctuary Policies: I will end all amnesty policies, defund sanctuary cities, and end outright the practice of transporting illegal migrants throughout the United States and dropping them into communities that are unprepared for them.
Deploy Military Assets: I will support the deployment of military assets to secure the border against the violent drug cartels and human trafficking rings.

| Peter,

**End Unfair Property Tax is proud to announce that the measure to end North Dakota’s unfair property tax has officially been approved by the Secretary of State and will appear on the November ballot as Measure #4!**

This success would not have been possible without the tireless dedication and hard work of our supporters, volunteers, and donors.

Measure #4 presents voters with an unprecedented opportunity to finally secure the tax relief and reform that the legislature had promised but failed to deliver.

**This measure ensures that cities, counties, and school districts retain complete control over their services**. It changes the source of funding for the local services we rely on, without reducing or eliminating that funding. Rest assured, we will not lose the services and providers we need.
---
[](https://endpropertytax.us4.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9d6930e918a0489c6f7d6bb50&id=ab9a4f1809&e=d842fb25cc)
[CLICK HERE TO HELP US END NORTH DAKOTA’S UNFAIR PROPERTY TAX THIS NOVEMBER >>>](https://endpropertytax.us4.list-manage.com/track/click?u=9d6930e918a0489c6f7d6bb50&id=548fb589c2&e=d842fb25cc)
| **Measure #4 requires the legislature to replace property tax at the current level** , meaning that everything you now pay in property tax, you will be able to keep.

We have a comprehensive plan for the state to replace the current property tax without cutting local funding, losing needed services, or raising taxes. North Dakota is uniquely positioned to achieve this.

Unfortunately, lobbyists and special interest groups have banded together to oppose the measure. **Their fearful claims about the measure are false**. We sincerely hope they will accept our offer to engage in a public forum or debate.

The property tax issue is of utmost importance to the people of North Dakota, and they deserve to have both sides fully presented and debated to make an informed decision at the voting booth.
**Help us combat the lies by selecting an option below and making a generous donation to our fight to END North Dakota’s unfair property tax today!

With your continued support, we will achieve meaningful tax relief and reform for all North Dakotans.

Sincerely,

**$7.** That’s all we’re asking from you to help elect Democrats in the states. Here’s why: **Reason #1:** Election Day is only 92 days away, and in November, we’re facing legislative elections in 44 states – $7 helps win races like those and more. **Reason #2:** We’re up against Trump and his MAGA movement who raised over $300 million last quarter alone. When enough grassroots Democrats chip in $7, it adds up and helps our candidates compete. **Reason #3:** Losing in November means Republicans will gain an advantage in key battleground states for years to come – $7 helps defeat extremists who are determined to attack abortion rights and access to the ballot. [So what do you say? # [#]
Friend,

I don’t think I’ll ever get tired of saying it: Thank you!

Just this week, our campaign faced a uniquely challenging fundraising deadline in the midst of what experts call “the summer slump” — a period where donations slow and critical momentum dies down.

3 months to Election Day and against an opponent fueled by national MAGA donors, that’s not something our campaign can afford — and Team Ruiz heard that loud and clear.

I’m proud to share that we hit (and exceeded) our fundraising goal! Thank you for your continued support in our mission to keep California’s 25th blue, and defend the progress we’ve made in Congress.

Your support is what carried us past our goal this week — and it’s exactly what’s going to lead us to victory come November. This isn’t a fight for one, or even two — defending the rights we hold dear will take all of us.

And together, we’ll do just that. If you didn’t get a chance to chip in before the deadline, don’t worry: you can still do so and make just as big of an impact by clicking here. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ruiz-em-fr-aug24?amount=]

Hi there, Today I am proud to endorse Kamala Harris for the next president of the United States. Not just because Donald Trump would be a disaster for our Democracy and our planet, but because she is the right person for the job. In her time as VP, she helped lead the strongest climate and environmental administration in recent history. I have faith in Kamala’s record of putting our planet & its people before corporate greed. And I have faith that she’ll fight to protect our Democracy, our rights, and a livable future. Well guess what, we're living through just such a moment, and I hope you can feel not just the excitement, but the possibility this moment holds, for each of us and for our planet. Before the Voting Rights Act of 1965 was passed, literacy tests and poll taxes prevented many people from exercising their right to vote.
When the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act in 2013, it took us back to that dark time of restricting the right to vote.

America is less safe as a result of this Harris-Biden betrayal. ---|--- | | | | | Years before her catastrophic failure as the Biden administration’s border czar, Vice President Kamala Harris helped an illegal alien become the nation’s first undocumented lawyer while she was California’s top law enforcement official. In a court brief filed during the illegal alien’s years-long legal battle to obtain a law license, then California Attorney General Harris wrote that “it is not a crime either to be present or to work in the United States without immigration status.” ---|--- | | | | | “The Biden Secret Service is in cover-up mode on its inexcusable and epic failure to protect former President Trump and other innocents,” said Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton. “For Secret Service leaders to promise transparency to Congress while hiding every possible FOIA record from the American people is yet another indictment of this corrupt and failing agency.” ---|--- | | | Washington Times Meanwhile, Judicial Watch filed a Federal Communications Commission complaint against NBCUniversal, which is broadcasting the games, for “airing obscene and indecent content from the Olympics Opening Ceremony.” The complaint noted that the drag queens were joined by child performers during a dance scene on a catwalk and in the “Last Supper” segment, even though the blue-painted Dionysius actor was nearly naked. Since Vice President Kamala Harris replaced Joe Biden on the Democratic ticket, the mainstream media has talked glowingly about “Kamala memes” and the enthusiastic support she’s received on social media.
**We wouldn’t blame you if you thought everyone on TikTok had become “coconut-pilled.”** 🥥
Yet that’s only half the story. Right-wing misinformation, conspiracies, and flat-out bigotry are spreading like wildfire about Kamala Harris on TikTok.
[**We’ll tell you how we’re fighting back in a moment, but if you’d like to support COURIER’s mission to stop right-wing extremism on social media, can you chip in $20 now?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/90264601/489942862/-593472309?refcode=20240805-EM-RightWingTikTok&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODQ5NDc0ZTctNWM1My1lZjExLTk5MWEtNjA0NWJkZGJmYzRiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=u8MN9RNAVLESHWYzpGqTEwYeXQFDrl2gf7lAhnTS5_A=)
It’s no secret that misinformation and extremism thrive on social media. But thanks to TikTok’s secretive and highly personalized algorithm, overtly racist and misogynistic attacks on Vice President Harris have thrived largely under the media’s radar. **Here are just a few examples of videos that have gained millions of views in recent days:**
* In a video that’s been viewed 1.5 million times, right-wing influencer Candace Owens claimed Kamala Harris “slept her way to the top.”
* Former Fox News personality Megyn Kelly’s video saying Harris is receiving Democratic support because Democrats “are not allowed to challenge a Black lady” has been viewed 1.3 million times.
* Tucker Carlson is using the platform to spread the racist insinuation that Harris, a former California AG, U.S. Senator, and Vice President, is a “DEI” pick undeserving of the nomination.

But it’s not just the influencers whose content is going viral on TikTok. Random accounts are doubling down and spreading more conspiracy theories to support Donald Trump’s baseless, racist claim that Kamala Harris somehow isn’t really Black.
This is where COURIER comes in. We understand how dangerous the right-wing’s racism and sexism are for our country. And we know that viral content on TikTok can have outsized importance in communities without access to factual, rigorous journalism.

When I was 21, I became pregnant. But I learned that with my aortic aneurysm, it would be impossible to carry the pregnancy to term.

**So, I had an abortion.**

I share my story because it’s not a secret, and it’s not shameful. I want the millions of people who’ve made the decision to seek abortion care to know they’re not alone.

My right to make the best decision for my health and future was protected by Roe v. Wade. Now, people in Tennessee and other GOP-controlled states are being denied that choice. It’s abhorrent.

The right to make our own reproductive health care decisions is fundamental. We cannot be equal if we don’t have control over our own bodies. The GOP wants to turn back the clock on every bit of progress generations have fought for, taking us back to a time before abortion was safe and legal.

I’ve listened to folks all over Tennessee, and here’s what I know: People want our communities to be safer, with access to birth control, IVF, and, yes, abortion.

**I’m running for U.S. Senate from Tennessee because we need more champions for abortion rights in Washington.** And when I get there, I won’t hesitate to use every power available to demand a restoration of our reproductive freedoms at the federal level. We have to secure our rights and prevent radicals like Marsha Blackburn from enacting a national ban.

clean_body: | When I was 21, I became pregnant. But I learned that with my aortic aneurysm, it would be impossible to carry the pregnancy to term. So, I had an abortion. I share my story because it’s not a secret, and it’s not shameful. I want the millions of people who’ve made the decision to seek abortion care to know they’re not alone. My right to make the best decision for my health and future was protected by Roe v. Wade. Now, people in Tennessee and other GOP-controlled states are being denied that choice. It’s abhorrent. The right to make our own reproductive health care decisions is fundamental. We cannot be equal if we don’t have control over our own bodies. The GOP wants to turn back the clock on every bit of progress generations have fought for, taking us back to a time before abortion was safe and legal. I’ve listened to folks all over Tennessee, and here’s what I know: People want our communities to be safer, with access to birth control, IVF, and, yes, abortion. I’m running for U.S. Senate from Tennessee because we need more champions for abortion rights in Washington. And when I get there, I won’t hesitate to use every power available to demand a restoration of our reproductive freedoms at the federal level. Peter, Right now you can’t scroll social media without seeing a news article or a hot take about Michigan’s role in the upcoming election. I have to say, as a Michigander, it’s flattering! But almost *all* of those stories are surrounding the presidential election. That’s obviously for good reason — we must, and will, win at the top of the ticket. And there are a LOT of other important elections happening in Michigan this year that are crucial to protecting our democracy, including for the state supreme court. **Michigan’s Republican candidates for state supreme court include three election deniers: one who attended a “Stop the Steal” rally at the state capitol on January 6, 2021; another who filed a lawsuit attempting to invalidate absentee ballots from Detroit; and another who’s facing four criminal felony charges for tampering with voting equipment.** **We’ve got to keep them off the bench, and we’re supporting two outstanding Democracy Defenders for the Michigan state supreme court: Justice Kyra Harris Bolden and Kimberly Ann Thomas.** [**Can we count on you to make a donation to the NDRC right away to help elect Democracy Defenders in Michigan and across the country?**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/90266103/489948136/-1472687013?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_ZoomMI_email_20240805-NDRC-Tier1-ZoomMI_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20240805-NDRC-Tier1-ZoomMI_&utm_campaign=ZoomMI&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjQ2OTBjZmIyLTVmNTMtZWYxMS05OTFhLTYwNDViZGRiZmM0YiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=K5ayTWV4D4E1HDadIHROc7VEksEblcIvCxCXX1CXbOc=) | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

subject: NYT Shapiro-Obama | Veepstakes| Comics for Kamala
body:
https://www.takingthehillpac.com/ [https://www.takingthehillpac.com/]
Friend,
Wanted to share with you this great New York Times piece on Josh Shapiro and the veepstakes. The article chronicles Governor Shapiro's relationship with President Obama, and how it has developed over the past two decades.
"In 2007, despite Mrs. Clinton's front-runner status for the Democratic nomination, Mr. Shapiro endorsed Mr. Obama for president, impressed by his promises to wind down the war in Iraq, said Mr. Murphy, who recalled discussing the decision with Mr. Shapiro."
“They became active campaigners on Mr. Obama’s behalf. Mr. Shapiro also drafted an open letter to the state’s Jewish community on behalf of Mr. Obama, after incendiary statements made by Mr. Obama’s former pastor had surfaced.
After Mr. Obama won the White House, Mr. Shapiro kept in touch with him and his political team.”
“Mr. Murphy, who went on to serve as an acting secretary of the Army in the Obama administration in 2016, sometimes played basketball with Mr. Obama. He recalled Mr. Shapiro’s name coming up.”
“Every time I would see him, he’s like, ‘How’s my guy Josh doing?’” Mr. Murphy said of his interactions with Mr. Obama. “All those folks in Obama’s orbit have a real soft spot for Josh Shapiro for doing what he did when it was not popular.”
As you all know, the veepstakes are heating up, with rumor noting the decision is down to between Governor Shapiro and Governor Walz, with Vice President Harris traveling to Philadelphia tomorrow for a rally to kick-off her tour through 2024's battleground states with her newly named Vice Presidential nominee.
Lastly, I wanted to invite you to join, attend, and contribute to Comics for Kamala tonight at 8pm! Join a star-studded cast of comics fighting the good fight for our democratic nominee!

name: Paul Buskirk for Congress
subject: Notes From Paul...'Tis the Season of County Fairs, Rodeos & Parades
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Buskirk for Congress campaign
body:
| | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/463fd9898fca/how-can-i-help-the-campaign-12700664?e=a3f26a61c6)
---
| A hallmark of our Kansas communities is how we celebrate one another. Summertime is the season of county fairs, rodeos, and especially parades!
As of this past weekend, I have had the blessing of participating in, one way or another, an abundance of these summer celebrations. My first parade was in Garden City during the Beef Empire Days in early June. It was a warm morning and I very much wanted to walk the parade route alongside the car where my campaign banners were displayed. It took me only a couple of blocks to realize, however, that my pace of greeting the parade watchers – and handing out lots of candy to the little ones – was not keeping up with my vehicle. As I ran out of my first bag of candy, I looked up to see my campaign car nearly a block ahead of me, along with the rest of the candy! A reminder, we can learn something every day!
---
| These midwestern celebrations often serve as a ‘grand equalizer’ in our communities. We gather together in our parks and fairgrounds and line up along parade routes to celebrate our communities along with long-standing heritage and traditions. We sing and dance with great performers. We hold our breath when the rodeo clown gets a push from the steer, or when the driver in the demolition derby side-swipes a wall! We eat some really great food and don’t worry at that moment if it’s good or bad for us. And we line the city streets and watch, wave, and smile as cars, trucks, flatbed trailers, and imposing farm equipment roll down the boulevard bearing friends and neighbors with banners, music, and candy!
---
| | | | | | | | | |
---
|
---
|
---
| We do all of this as a community – without worry about ideologies. The candidate in the car running for public office waves at the folks on the curb. And then?....they wave back – every time! If you haven’t participated in a parade, I can assure you it is nearly impossible not to smile with people of all ages waving and smiling back at you!
We have so much more in common than the extreme voices want us to believe.
---
| There are more great community celebrations yet to take place this summer. There is still time to find cotton candy, corn dogs, and the famous deep-fried butter!
As we move towards important election days, let us keep this sense of community in mind. As we communicate with others with different views and as we ponder who is best to serve our communities, let us put aside ideology and focus on the needs of the people.
**And most of all ...Don't forget to vote!**

---
| **MANY voices. ONE passion.****UNITED to provide a legacy for our children.**
---
|

Of all of the things I have done as Governor of California, the one thing I wasn't prepared at the start was San Quentin.

Of all of the things I have done as Governor of California, the one thing I wasn't prepared for at the start was San Quentin.
But since then, we have taken the steps to transform San Quentin — the state’s most notorious prison with a dark past — into the nation’s most innovative rehabilitation prison focused on building a brighter and safer future.
Last week, I went inside San Quentin — behind the scenes and behind the walls — with my friends Marshawn "Beast Mode" Lynch and Doug Hendrickson as part of our Politickin' Podcast.
[**Please use this link to listen to (or save for later) a very real and raw discussion with the prison's warden, guards, and inmates — including one I played Little League baseball with — about life behind the walls of San Quentin.**](https://podcasts.apple.com/ca/podcast/politickin-with-gavin-newsom-marshawn-lynch-and/id1755262381?source=em240805-1-subs)

name: AOC
subject: Vice President
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
On Instagram recently, someone asked if I could shed some light on what the selection process for the Vice Presidential nominee might look like right now.
I won’t speak to the _current_ process because of the first point that I’ll make: the VP selection process — unlike the Presidential selection process, which is very public facing — is often a very personal, private decision.
It starts with your Presidential nominee trying to figure out what they prioritize in a Vice President. There’s a lot of things that need to be balanced: **what is going to be electorally successful, but also what kind of governance partner do you want?**
I would imagine that someone like VP Harris, having served as a Vice President, is taking this decision very, very seriously in a lot of different dimensions.
Another thing to consider is that, once you do get some finalists, those people will go through some of the most rigorous vetting and opposition research known to man. That is done to know every single vulnerability that the other side might exploit, to either (if it’s bad) filter you out or (if you’re selected) prepare for.
**But sometimes, the VP selection sends a message**.
President Biden, for example, served in the Senate for decades. He really, really valued the importance of mastering the Senate, and understood the importance of having a governing partner who mastered the Senate, in order to help pass legislation. I think his selection of VP Harris communicates that.
**President Trump’s selection of J.D. Vance, for example, indicates and communicates to the public that they hate women**.
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20240805.hWQGMc&refcode=em20240805-6943-P_FND_CTR_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=6943%2E2526796%2EMgmZSU)
The cynics say that we must resign ourselves to a Trump-Vance White House. They will tell you one vote won't change anything. **But change isn't up the cynics — it's up to us.** [Will you make a contribution of $5 today to power our movement’s fight against Trump's extremism? Without a concerted effort to combat the MAGA movement, right-wing extremists will endanger marginalized communities and our democracy itself.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20240805.hWQGMc&refcode=em20240805-6943-P_FND_CTR_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=6943%2E2526796%2EMgmZSU) **[Contribute $5](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20240805.hWQGMc&refcode=em20240805-6943-P_FND_CTR_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=6943%2E2526796%2EMgmZSU)**

clean_body: On Instagram recently, someone asked if I could shed some light on what the selection process for the Vice Presidential nominee might look like right now. I won’t speak to the current process because of the first point that I’ll make: the VP selection process — unlike the Presidential selection process, which is very public facing — is often a very personal, private decision. It starts with your Presidential nominee trying to figure out what they prioritize in a Vice President. There’s a lot of things that need to be balanced: what is going to be electorally successful, but also what kind of governance partner do you want? I would imagine that someone like VP Harris, having served as a Vice President, is taking this decision very, very seriously in a lot of different dimensions. Another thing to consider is that, once you do get some finalists, those people will go through some of the most rigorous vetting and opposition research known to man. That is done to know every single vulnerability that the other side might exploit, to either (if it’s bad) filter you out or (if you’re selected) prepare for. But sometimes, the VP selection sends a message. President Biden, for example, served in the Senate for decades. He really, really valued the importance of mastering the Senate, and understood the importance of having a governing partner who mastered the Senate, in order to help pass legislation. I think his selection of VP Harris communicates that. President Trump’s selection of J.D. Vance, for example, indicates and communicates to the public that they hate women. The cynics say that we must resign ourselves to a Trump-Vance White House. They will tell you one vote won't change anything. But change isn't up the cynics — it's up to us. In solidarity, Alexandria | ---|--- | | ---|---|--- Email us: mailto: speak@ocasiocortez.com

body:
I know we’ve sent a number of emails your way. But with our primary election over and the general election kicking off, I hope you understand that we’re not doing it to annoy you.
#

Peter, it’s Ruben Gallego here.
I know we’ve sent a number of emails your way. But with our primary election over and the general election kicking off, I hope you understand that we’re not doing it to annoy you.
We’re sending them because emails like this are one of the single, biggest ways we fund a campaign that can win.
And today, I am asking if there is anything, anything at all that I can say to convince you to chip in to my campaign.
**What if I told you that this will be one of the most closely contested, most expensive, most decisive elections in the entire country this year** — and that we MUST win to hold the U.S. Senate?
**What if I told you that Trump attacked me — personally, by name — during a rally with Kari Lake?** If we’re going to defeat Trump and stop him from retaking the White House, it starts right here in Arizona.
**And what if I told you that your support really, truly matters. Seriously.** I’ve seen what this team can do, and with less than 100 days to go until the most important election of our lifetime, your donation is absolutely critical to our success.
Please, Peter. A lot of people have already chipped in to help us reach our goals and they’re hoping you'll do the same. We are, too.
[**Can I count on you to chip in $5, or whatever you can afford today, to my campaign for U.S. Senate in Arizona? ## Early Vote Starts TODAY!

Dear Friends,

**Early voting starts TODAY, August 5th!**

This is our chance to make a real difference and steer our state towards a brighter future.

Mary Peltola has voted against ANWR, Alaskan resource development, veterans, and parents. She even supports non-citizen voting. We need to reclaim Alaska’s seat from the radical left and bring true representation back to our great state. The decisions made in Congress impact our daily lives, and it’s crucial to have someone who truly represents Alaskan values and priorities.

I believe in Alaska’s potential and am committed to ensuring our story is powerfully represented in Congress. By voting early, you'll have time to share the importance of this election with your family, friends, neighbors, and coworkers. Your early vote not only counts but also sets an example for others, showing the strength and unity of our community.

Thank you for your support and your vote. Together, we can replace Peltola and ensure that Alaska is represented well once again. Let’s stand up for our values, our resources, and our future. This election is about making sure our voices are heard and our needs are met in Washington.

**America First, Fighting for Alaska!**

Best regards,

Nick Begich

body:
The countdown is on.
|
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/90273479/489973494/-1505231027?refcode=ODP_ATA_EM_FR_ThreeMonths_240805_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTI0NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YjliZDQ0Ny03MzUzLWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRkYmZjNGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fxdh2317Lbnbe3GSJWCHnkO5sUgNrymY3w64RRss5xI=) Team,

We know it’s hard to believe but we’re officially 3 months out from Election Day – **the most important election in Ohio’s history.** And boy do we have a lot of work to do.

We’re gearing up for this final stretch and we can’t afford to lose our momentum. Before we tell you why, [_**we have to ask: exactly 3 months before Election Day, can you chip in $3?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/90273481/489973496/-1505231027?amount=3&refcode=ODP_ATA_EM_FR_ThreeMonths_240805_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTI0NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YjliZDQ0Ny03MzUzLWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRkYmZjNGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fxdh2317Lbnbe3GSJWCHnkO5sUgNrymY3w64RRss5xI=)

Here’s what’s at stake this year:
1. **Senate control:** Sherrod Brown’s seat will decide Senate control. But as one of the most vulnerable senators in the entire country, Mitch McConnell and D.C. Republicans are funneling millions of dollars into Ohio to flip his seat (it’s already the nation’s most expensive race). What we do NOW to fight back will have a huge impact on what happens on Election Day.
2. **House control:** That’s right. Not only will Ohio decide control of the Senate, but our state is home to some of the most competitive Congressional races in the country – three tossup seats that are key to flipping the House blue and deciding the fate of the GOP’s out-of-touch agenda.
3. **Ohio Supreme Court control:** Last but certainly not least, we’re the only state in the country with the chance to flip its Supreme Court. The current Republican-controlled court has been a tool for the GOP to mold the law to fit their political agendas – rubber stamping gerrymandered maps, obstructing our abortion rights amendment, you name it.

Look, we know winning in 3 months isn’t going to be easy. In fact, it’s going to take a pretty massive effort from _all of us._

We have staff to hire, merch to design, yard signs to deliver, volunteers to recruit, and hundreds of thousands of Ohio voters to talk to before the big day. And we’re confident we can do it with your support.

[_**Our time to make an impact is running short. Please, if you can, donate anything you are able to help elect Ohio Democrats up and down the ballot in 3 months >>>**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/90273483/489973498/-1505231027?refcode=ODP_ATA_EM_FR_ThreeMonths_240805_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTI0NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5YjliZDQ0Ny03MzUzLWVmMTEtOTkxYS02MDQ1YmRkYmZjNGIiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=fxdh2317Lbnbe3GSJWCHnkO5sUgNrymY3w64RRss5xI=)

body:
I’m supporting Lucas Kunce for Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat. Will you join me?
#
[ ](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65530?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY)
Hi Peter, it’s Jon Hamm.
I’m a born-and-raised Missourian who watched with horror when Josh Hawley raised his fist at insurrectionists outside the U.S. Capitol on January 6th, then ran out the back door when they stormed the building later that day.
I’ve seen communities across my home state torn apart because of cowardly politicians like him — and I’m not willing to sit on the sidelines in this election.
So before [**make a donation of $10 or whatever you can today toward my friend Lucas Kunce’s campaign to replace Josh Hawley,**](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65530?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY) please let me tell you why:
**[SUPPORT LUCAS KUNCE →](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65530?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY)**
Most of my family is from a town in Missouri called Ste. Genevieve, about 60 miles south of St. Louis. I’ve watched their community go downhill for years.
While corrupt politicians shipped jobs overseas and voted to give handouts to Wall Street and their corporate allies, everyday people just trying to survive in the place they call home ran out of money and opportunities.
**Our leaders abandoned them — and Josh Hawley is the perfect example.**
Instead of fighting for what would make the communities in my home state stronger, Josh Hawley has been busy engaging in the out-of-touch culture wars that only divide us — all so he can get more and more power for himself.
That’s what we saw on January 6th, 2021. Hawley raised his fist at rioters outside the Capitol because he thought it would make himself look strong. But when sh*t got real, he ran out the back door like a coward — away from the same people he was claiming to support just hours earlier.
What’s even more ridiculous? Since that day, Hawley has desperately tried to convince all of us that he’s the authority on what it means to be a man in this country. He even published a whole book about it last year:
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65530?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY)
Well... when I think about manhood, I think about courage. And that’s not something you can write a book about.
Missouri is the Show Me State. Courage is something you have to show us.
**That’s why I’m supporting Lucas Kunce for Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat.** As a born-and-raised Missourian who joined the Marines to serve the community that took care of him growing up, Lucas has already shown us that he knows the true meaning of courage.
Lucas knows courage is about standing up to the powerful and working to rebuild our state. And he knows real leaders fight to empower everyday people and secure our future for generations to come — not for their own power or profit.
**So Peter, if you want to be told about manhood, some guy wrote a book about it.[But if you want someone to show you real courage, please join me in supporting Lucas Kunce for U.S. Senate by making a donation of $10 toward his grassroots campaign today.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65530?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY) **
If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution instantly:
[Contribute $10](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65531?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=10&t=6&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY) [Contribute $25](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65531?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=7&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY) [Contribute $30](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65531?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=30&t=8&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY) [Contribute $50](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65531?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=50&t=9&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY) [Contribute $100](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65531?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=100&t=10&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY) [Contribute $250](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65531?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=250&t=11&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY) [Give another amount](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/65530?refcode=em20240805-7258&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=12&akid=7258%2E614464%2EQE7cpY)

* * *
Peter, it’s Travis with VoteVets.
By this point you’ve probably heard of the PACT Act. And if you’ve been with VoteVets for a while, you’ve _definitely_ heard of it. If you’ve got a minute, would you let me explain why the PACT Act is going to be so important this year, and what we are going to do to make sure it’s top of mind when Veterans go to the polls in November?
For generations, the men and women who served our country around the world suffered toxic exposures. From Agent Orange in Vietnam to burn pits in Iraq and Afghanistan. And for generations, Veterans went without the care they needed to handle the impacts of those toxic exposures. Many of you are Veterans like me, or you come from Military Families. We know these folks.
Year after year, Congress after Congress, bills went up to provide this care. Year after year, Republicans shot it down. Trump talked a big game — he never got it done. But President Biden’s son was one of the Vets who suffered and died after a toxic exposure. This was a priority for him. It took a coalition led by the President, Democrats, VoteVets, and our allies to get the PACT Act across the finish line last year, and even that came after Republicans in the Senate shot it down and dragged their feet.
It took too long. We lost too many of our brothers and sisters to get here, but we got it done — and that matters. To quote the President, "it’s a Big F’ing Deal". As of today more than a million claims have been filed and granted and more are coming in all the time. The PACT Act was the right thing to do, but I’ll be damned if we don’t make sure that Veterans around the country know that it is Democrats who got this done while Republicans stood in the way.
Starting on August 6th, we’re going to be busing Veterans around the country to talk about the PACT Act. Coast to coast, we’re going to battleground states and districts to support our friends and allies in tough races — the leaders who got this done. The goal is to raise awareness, drive media, and bring Veterans and Military Families on side. We’re going to make some noise here, and we need your help to make sure people hear us.
Big programs like this are not cheap, but VoteVets is one of the only organizations in the country with the infrastructure, the knowledge, and the resources to make it happen. This will make a difference, but we need your help.

| Friends,
Earlier today it was reported that Susan Wild has been caught — once again — making outlandish comments online, this time by suggesting that agitators pay a “visit” to a U.S. Senator at his home. Unfortunately, Susan Wild seems to spend her time disparaging constituents and attacking those she doesn't agree with instead of working on fixing the issues that are facing everyday Americans.

Susan Wild suggested that his address should be on a billboard, and then went on to say that people should pay him a “visit.” Read the story [here.](https://mackenzieforcongress.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=62252a4538e3fe848298033c5&id=32a38314ce&e=5ccada9200)
Please share this with your friends and family so they know who Susan Wild really is because she will be coming after me next. She will attack and smear me so she can hold onto power.

That means printing out campaign literature to hand to folks on the doors, making sure our volunteers are staying hydrated out in the summer sun, and putting up digital ads left and right to share the message of our campaign early on.
All of this and more is critical to our mobilization efforts, and getting it done early is the key to success come November. | | Friend, My heart is breaking for Officer Daniel Sanchez, and I need your help to keep him out of prison and with his wife and family where he belongs. You see, Daniel is facing a decade behind bars because he followed his training and defended himself and others against a deadly threat. Because of the political motivations of one anti-cop prosecutor, Daniel’s life could be ruined... ...and to top it all off, Daniel’s wife is now pregnant with their first child. This little family that is just starting could be ripped apart unjustly! **[**Please consider sending an urgent gift of $35 to help us defend Daniel against the baseless charges against him that could land him in prison for TEN YEARS.**](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8jkFv4yAQRn_N-IZFBgzOgUN2I-9hq957qoAZJ1QmdjBpmn9fOap6nXn63vN5mdL4cGD_AOI50QqIoA6AeH2753L7yP__iYN9OYmrec3d9sW_gFgfC_-iPystZ5-m7WqPDTk1ktQNu51F7Pe2N6Y5Ox13plOh05ZI6tiPZPcckLox2mAxNMmhRC172SFqJbE1vvNW6xDJqhHDCFo-Pa3PXFL0u7XefSnznNs452Zy51qX9Rk2AA4rx1vh1l-Y5roRgMMlLgQ4UBAVSXAWRgv-qqCGdb6VyO9xJgZ1pCA2VHA2OggpVVMcLfc0TWk1FrQ8PUM27afD7wAAAP__VclkwA)** In 2020, Jose Garza campaigned for District Attorney of Travis County, Texas, with a goal. Not to prosecute criminals, not to protect the community he was elected to serve...but to go after cops who risk their lives every day to help citizens like you and me stay safe. When Garza got elected, he made good on his promise and began prosecuting police officers one after another, even digging up old cases to prove a political point. Officers like Daniel Sanchez are being caught in the crosshairs of a battle they didn’t agree to and don’t deserve. Now Daniel is facing the possibility of ten years in prison.
---
[](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8jkFv4yAQRn_N-IZFBgzOgUN2I-9hq957qoAZJ1QmdjBpmn9fOap6nXn63vN5mdL4cGD_AOI50QqIoA6AeH2753L7yP__iYN9OYmrec3d9sW_gFgfC_-iPystZ5-m7WqPDTk1ktQNu51F7Pe2N6Y5Ox13plOh05ZI6tiPZPcckLox2mAxNMmhRC172SFqJbE1vvNW6xDJqhHDCFo-Pa3PXFL0u7XefSnznNs452Zy51qX9Rk2AA4rx1vh1l-Y5roRgMMlLgQ4UBAVSXAWRgv-qqCGdb6VyO9xJgZ1pCA2VHA2OggpVVMcLfc0TWk1FrQ8PUM27afD7wAAAP__VclkwA)
---
Why? In November 2022, the officer responded to a house call where a man was firing shots into a house indiscriminately. Daniel shouted to the suspect, who had already fired two shots into the house, to drop his gun. When the suspect refused, Daniel had no other choice but to fire his weapon to stop the imminent danger to himself and to the innocent people in the densely populated neighborhood. Within a minute of being shot by Daniel, police officers performed life-saving measures on the suspect but were unsuccessful in saving him. Now, Daniel is the one being treated like a common criminal. **[I pray you’ll consider donating to Officer Daniel Sanchez’s defense with a gift of $35 or more today to help us hire the best lawyers possible to defend him.](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8jkFv4yAQRn_N-IZFBgzOgUN2I-9hq957qoAZJ1QmdjBpmn9fOap6nXn63vN5mdL4cGD_AOI50QqIoA6AeH2753L7yP__iYN9OYmrec3d9sW_gFgfC_-iPystZ5-m7WqPDTk1ktQNu51F7Pe2N6Y5Ox13plOh05ZI6tiPZPcckLox2mAxNMmhRC172SFqJbE1vvNW6xDJqhHDCFo-Pa3PXFL0u7XefSnznNs452Zy51qX9Rk2AA4rx1vh1l-Y5roRgMMlLgQ4UBAVSXAWRgv-qqCGdb6VyO9xJgZ1pCA2VHA2OggpVVMcLfc0TWk1FrQ8PUM27afD7wAAAP__VclkwA)** The thing is, NCPD doesn’t receive a dime from the federal government – 100% of our funding comes from private donations. While Jose Garza has power and government funding on his side, we’re starting from scratch to fund the defense of public servants who don’t have hundreds in thousands of dollars in savings for legal battles like this. This truly is a David and Goliath situation – and not only is one man’s future on the line, but the future of his wife and unborn child are in jeopardy. It’s going to take the best lawyers available to defend him against, and that comes at a hefty cost. **[Please don’t delay in giving $35, $50, $100, or whatever you can spare to provide Daniel with the expert defense he needs and deserves.](https://email.email.america1stwarroom.com/c/eJw8jkFv4yAQRn_N-IZFBgzOgUN2I-9hq957qoAZJ1QmdjBpmn9fOap6nXn63vN5mdL4cGD_AOI50QqIoA6AeH2753L7yP__iYN9OYmrec3d9sW_gFgfC_-iPystZ5-m7WqPDTk1ktQNu51F7Pe2N6Y5Ox13plOh05ZI6tiPZPcckLox2mAxNMmhRC172SFqJbE1vvNW6xDJqhHDCFo-Pa3PXFL0u7XefSnznNs452Zy51qX9Rk2AA4rx1vh1l-Y5roRgMMlLgQ4UBAVSXAWRgv-qqCGdb6VyO9xJgZ1pCA2VHA2OggpVVMcLfc0TWk1FrQ8PUM27afD7wAAAP__VclkwA)** I’ll make sure Daniel and his wife know that you donated, and I know they’ll be so happy to hear they have your support during this difficult time. Gratefully, Jim Fotis
